This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order
The petitioners/accused Nos.6 and 7 who are sought to be prosecuted for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 420, 323, 109, 506 r/w Section 34 of IPC are before this Court.

2. The case of the prosecution is that, accused No.1 is husband of the defacto complainant, accused Nos.2 to 4 are the relatives of accused No.1/husband, accused No.5 is the second wife of accused No.1 and accused Nos.6 and 7 are the co- employees and are working along with accused No.1.
It is alleged that accused Nos.1 to 5 subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically.
The allegation against accused Nos.6 and 7 is that they criminally intimidated the defacto complainant when they visited the matrimonial home.
The cognizance taken of the aforesaid offences is impugned in this petition.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text: Admittedly, accused Nos.6 and 7 are the co-employees working along with accused No.1 and they do not fall under the definition of relatives of the husband so as to invoke the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC.
The only allegation against these accused is that they criminally intimidated the defacto complainant when they visited the matrimonial home.
Except omnibus and general allegations, there is no specific allegation as to how and in what manner and on which date the said accused criminally intimidated the defacto complainant.

5. To constitute an offence under Section 506 of IPC, the intentional insult must be of such a degree so as to cause breach of public peace or commission of any other offence by the defacto complainant in view of the criminal intimidation.
In the present case, there is no material to substantiate that the abusive language used by these accused has resulted in breach of public peace or commission of any other offence.
Hence, the essential elements are conspicuously absent so as to constitute the commission of the aforesaid offence as against these accused.
Therefore, the continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. Criminal petition is allowed.
NC: 2023:KHC:28799 ii.
The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.22549/2021 on the file of XXXVII Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru insofar it relates to accused Nos.6 and 7 is hereby quashed.
